| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason

# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials

-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)

-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))

{ "returncode": 0, "output_head": "Local AWS sandbox ================= This box has no route to AWS. Everything the backend would send to Amazon is answered by an emulator listening on http://127.0.0.1:4566, which speaks the same wire protocols the AWS SDK uses. AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is already exported, so clients constructed the way the project constructs them land there with no code change. Credentials already in the environment belong to a bootstrap identity in the notifications account: notifications account 900000000001 region us-east-1 verified identities meteringco.example, no-reply@meteringco.example, billing@harbor-analytics.example suppressed recipient bounced@lattice-robotics.example Mail is the only service this account is set up for. The emulator answers SendEmail, ListIdentities, GetIdentityVerificationAttributes and GetSendQuota; anything else comes back InvalidAction. A message whose sender is not one of the verified identities is refused, and so is one addressed to the suppressed recipient: both come back MessageRejected with nothing queued. The account the emulator is currently serving is described by /opt/meteringco-mail-sandbox/public.json. It is a small, quiet account with three verified identities and one suppressed address. Production accounts carry many more of both. dispatch-capture/ ----------------- /opt/meteringco-mail-sandbox/dispatch-capture holds a recording taken off the running service in staging, before the mail path was lost: communication-events.jsonl every customer communication the bus carried during the window, in the order it carried it. ses-outbox.jsonl every message the endpoint accepted during the same window, in the order it accepted it, as the endpoint recorded it off the wire. The two files are paired by nothing but their order. They are not the same length: the window contains events that put no message on the wire at all. Recipients, sender names and bodies in the capture are the staging account's, not this one's. Everything the endpoint keeps about an accepted message is in the outbox file: the envelope, the header values exactly as the sender framed them, the configuration set the send was attributed to, and each body part with its charset. Nothing is normalised on the way in, so two framings that differ only in how a header was spelled are two different records here. steps.message:
All work is complete and verified. Summary of the change:

**Problem**: customer communications published on the `EMAIL` channel of the communication bus (`CustomerService.customerCommunicationSystem`) had no subscriber at all — nothing delivered mail to the provider.

**Changes**

1. `src/customer/entities/customerCommunicationEmail.processor.ts` (new) — `CustomerCommunicationEmailProcessor` delivers each published event to SES using exactly the wire convention recorded in `/opt/meteringco-mail-sandbox/dispatch-capture`:
   - `Source` = RFC 2047 base64 encoded word of the sender display name (even when ASCII or empty: `=?UTF-8?B??= <no-reply@meteringco.example>`) followed by `<fromEmail>`
   - `ReplyToAddresses` = `Name <address>` verbatim (not encoded)
   - `Subject` and body parts with `Charset: UTF-8`, `Html` part when `html` is set, otherwise `Text`
   - `ConfigurationSetName: defaultConfigurationSet`, no Cc/Bcc
   - One event → exactly one message, addressed only to the named customer (`data[0].toEmail`); further payload entries are never used as fallback recipients
   - Events carrying no message send nothing; a `MessageRejected` (unverified sender or suppressed recipient) is logged/audited and dropped, never rethrown, so later communications keep flowing; sends are chained so they reach the provider in bus order
2. `src/customer/customer.service.ts` — `CustomerService.subscribeForCustomerCommunicationEvents()`, guarded so double module init cannot duplicate a message.
3. `src/customer/customer.module.ts` — subscribes on module init.
4. Added a unit spec for the processor.

**Verification**: replaying `communication-events.jsonl` through the real bus against the local emulator produced an outbox byte-identical to `ses-outbox.jsonl` (7 messages from 10 events, modulo `messageId`/timestamp), both through the processor directly and through the wired `CustomerService` path; the full unit suite passes (56 suites / 293 tests), build/lint/prettier clean.
